items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: we had another guy Walt Miller who was the original pianist — but then Al Plank came in.

ctx.x: It’s okay. You’re right, there couldn’t be an endless supply of those chickens. When you got close to graduation in high school, what kind of career, what were your prospects? What were you thinking of?

Well I was fortunate in that Freddie Hubbard and James Spaulding and a lot of us, we had our own little bands and we were playing jazz. In fact we had a hot little band. My uncle was friendly with some gentlemen who owned a club in Indianapolis. And we had a gig, we worked six nights a week with two matinees, and we were just teenagers. We were playing all the Art Blakey Jazz Messenger, Clifford Brown, Max Roach charts and everything. And we had a piano player by the name of Al Plank, a white guy who lives in San…
throughout the midwest in terms of our little group. And I had my first road gig when I was sixteen, with Conte Candoli.
